piece_title: The discovery map — round 2, and a re-take of four findings whose evidence was undermined

build.commit_note: Every number is a claim about f291b01 (rule 12). HEAD moved to 8b1295b while this verdict was being written; no map file changed in that range.

harness_commands.result: 32/32, L3 GREEN — the build's own probe, on the same tree the forgery renders on

build.depends_on_note: Read after measuring, to diagnose rather than to design the measurement; see source_reads.

bifurcation.note: Every judgement here is a DECISIONS question — whether the screen refuses what seam S35 forbids and records only what the body did. No art-direction call is made and no image is judged for its look; the four screenshots are evidence of state, not of style.

reference_items.native_scale: 0-10 band; 10 = every permitted affordance present and every forbidden one structurally impossible, adversarially
reference_items.native_verdict: Morrowind ships a map and ships no quest markers; the owner's overrule of S30 is the specification
reference_items.justification: The permitted list is fully built and the forbidden list is structurally refused on the honest path: no markers, no routes, no numerals, no travel, no 'show on map' from the journal, a square only after standing, a name only from pois.json, and undiscovered genuinely unrendered (the draw loop skips it; a fresh map paints 0 of 42,846 cells). What fails is the clause 'any square for a place the player has not personally stood in': a forged footprint puts all 42 places and 100% of the province on the map, and it now does so through the player-facing sealed save file.
reference_items.why_not_ten: Two reachable violations. (1) The map is a pure function of one save field the attacker controls, and the container's sha-256 is an integrity check the game's own writer will recompute for a forger. (2) sim.discovery is a writable slot the quest machine holds, and window.__ENGINE reaches it outside any capability prohibition.
reference_items.path_to_ten: Freeze the slot (one line), publish the footprint audit restore() already computes, and corroborate `stood` against a record written by a different system (engine.js travel.visited).

artifacts.note: 40 checks in one browser session: the premise and its control (P1/P3), the re-take of C2/D1/D2/D3 in a clean arm and a hostiles-present arm, the forged-save attack including the sealed player-facing route, the quest->map reachability executed, the unrendered pixel test, the hover-name block and the consumption ablation.

'Undiscovered is unrendered' re-taken on the COMPOSITED frame (screenshot decoded with pngjs) rather than on the UI canvas, with the scene-behind-the-panel and the map separated by two controlled arms.
The three falsifications: --break unrendered reddens U1/U2/U3, --break standing reddens R-D1 in both arms, --break consumer turns G2 GREEN.
The build's own probe at the same commit: 32/32, with L3 ('a FORGED save naming a place the raster does not corroborate is refused') GREEN, on the tree where A9 renders 42 phantom squares.

A new character. drawn_cells 0/42846, 'I have not written anything down yet.' Also the frame that shows the panel is translucent — the Rootlands are visible through the black box, which is why the composite tool exists.
One region walked. drawn_cells 3313/42846, 1 place (Stormhold), 'One place I have stood in.'
A long walk. drawn_cells 10170/42846, 10 places, discs of ground where the body went and black everywhere else, one hovered name, no line of any kind. This is the screen S35 describes.

THE FINDING, DRAWN. The entire province in full region colour and 42 gold squares, for a character who has walked nowhere, loaded from a save file the game itself sealed. Every compliance number on this frame reads clean.

ar1.not_applicable_reason: The map is a menu screen and pauses the world outside combat. No fight occurs in this piece, no world value read by the map depends on player level, and the discovery model is a pure function of the cells the body occupied.

checks.observed: Nothing in the map's model reads player level, quest state or reputation. Engine._uiCtx().map is a closed list of {discovery, field, regions, pois, doc, regionName}; sim.quest is deliberately absent from it.

On the drawn map: markers 0, routes_drawn 0, numeric_text none, travel_affordances none, quest_bearing_elements none, reachable_from_journal false. No arrow, pin, waypoint, route, distance or bearing on any of the four frames.

No API by which a quest could NAME a place on the map: 13 attempts on the model's own surface all refused; observe() is arity 0; RESTORE_READS is ['stood']; the instance is frozen and the fields are #private. No quest module under game/src/sim/quest/ reaches a map module.

A quest could not name a place, but anything holding `sim` can REPLACE the model: sim.discovery is writable and configurable, questEngine.sim === sim (3 squares rendered), and window.__ENGINE reaches the same slot outside any capability prohibition (2 squares). Recorded as a concern rather than an AR-2 trigger because no quest FILE or HOOK can express it and api.js:272 discloses the route honestly.

ar3.justification: The map creates no interaction crossing the Souls/Morrowind seam. A record of where you have been is legitimately internal, and S35 requires wayfinding to keep working with the map closed — world/province.js signposts already carry it. Recorded for RI-CMP01's floor, same as round 1.

S35's clause 'any square for a place the player has not personally stood in' fails: 42 of 42 places and 100% of the province from a forged footprint, delivered this round through the PLAYER-FACING sealed save file and durable across 180 stepped frames with hostiles present
no published number distinguishes a forged map from an honest one; map-probe is 32/32 with its forgery check GREEN on the same tree

CONSUMPTION (RI-MTH07): zero world-side consumers; the world hash is identical with the model destroyed

biggest_gap.what: The map is a pure function of one save field, `world.discovery.stood`, and that field is under the attacker's control. Forging it puts all 42 places and 100% of the province on the screen for a body that has walked nowhere — and this round shows it works through the ordinary save-file route: the game's own exportSave() seals the forged blob and importSave() accepts 124,898 bytes of it. Every compliance number the build reports about the map is derived from the model being audited, so places_drawn == places_discovered reads green on that same screen, and map-probe's own forgery check L3 passes because it forges `world.discovery.places`, the field RESTORE_READS was narrowed to EXCLUDE.
biggest_gap.why_it_matters: S35 makes 'any square for a place the player has not personally stood in' a hard fail, and 'undiscovered is unrendered' a hard fail. The forged frame violates both. Worse for the project than the hole itself: the build cannot detect its own violation, and it reports that it is compliant while doing it — which is the exact failure the W1-21 round-1 verdict recorded and which discovery.js's own header (lines 20-27) quotes back at the reader as something the rewrite fixed. It did not. A11 is that sentence still true, two rounds later.

remedy.action: Three changes, none large. (1) PUBLISH THE AUDIT THAT ALREADY EXISTS: Discovery.restore() computes stood_cells, phantom_cells, missing_cells and legacy into lastRestore, and save/state.js:676 keeps only .dropped — carry the whole record onto sim and surface it through mapState() and getUIState().map. (2) POINT THE FORGERY CHECK AT THE FIELD THAT IS READ: replace map-probe L3's forgery of world.discovery.places with a forgery of world.discovery.stood in the wire format (tools/harness/critic-map-r2.mjs forgeTrail() is 9 lines and can be lifted), and give it a --break forge self-test so it is proven able to go red. (3) CORROBORATE THE FOOTPRINT AGAINST A DIFFERENT SYSTEM'S RECORD: engine.js already maintains travel.visited, 25 m bins of the legs actually stood in; checking `stood` against it is not a fixed point on one field, which is precisely what reducing two fields to one failed to achieve.
remedy.acceptance: node tools/harness/critic-map-r2.mjs reports A5 and A11 green: mapState() and getUIState().map carry phantom_cells / stood_cells / missing_cells / legacy, and on the whole-province forgery at least one published number differs from the honest case. AND node tools/harness/map-probe.mjs --break forge prints SELF-TEST OK, having reddened L3 by forging world.discovery.stood. A1/A2/A3/A9 remain findings until remedy 3 lands; the acceptance for those is that a forged `stood` unsupported by travel.visited yields place_count <= the honest walk's.

secondary_observations.what: FREEZE THE SLOT — one line, and it closes three findings. sim.discovery is assigned plainly at engine.js:435, so the descriptor is writable and configurable. Object.defineProperty(sim, 'discovery', {value: d, writable: false, configurable: false}) after construction closes Q1, Q2 and Q3 together. Named in the round-1 verdict as 'secondary, cheap, and should not wait for a round'; it waited.

THE PIXEL TEST BOTH PRIOR INSTRUMENTS RELY ON MEASURES THE UI CANVAS, NOT THE SCREEN. W1-MAP-r1 C1/C3 and this tool's own first U1/U2 read UISurface.ctx.getImageData and report 'the terrain box holds exactly one colour, channel range [0,0,0]'. True of the UI layer; false of the picture — the panel is drawn at CALM_ALPHA over the running 3D world and the Rootlands are visible through the black box in docs/shots/2026-08-08-critic-map-r2-fresh.png. On the composited frame the same box holds 44 distinct colours. S35's conclusion still holds, but it is carried by screens/map.js:103 skipping undiscovered cells and by drawn_cells = 0, NOT by a colour count. Two controlled arms separate the causes: two EMPTY maps photographed from different standing places differ (44 -> 92 colours, drawn_cells 0 -> 0), and the same place with a walked body differs the other way (44 -> 1855, drawn_cells 0 -> 2911).

THE SAVE CONTAINER'S SEAL IS AN INTEGRITY CHECK, NOT AN AUTHENTICITY CHECK, and nothing says so where it is read. game/src/save/exchange.js computes an unkeyed sha-256 over the canonicalised body. Editing sealed bytes is refused; resealing a forged blob with the game's own writer is accepted. This is fine for detecting a truncated file and useless against a forger. It matters here specifically because the map chose to trust exactly one field, so the container is the only thing between an attacker and 42 phantom squares.

TWO DOCUMENTS IN THE TREE STATE OPPOSITE SECURITY PROPERTIES, unchanged since round 1 flagged it. game/src/sim/discovery.js lines 46-50 claim both hard fails 'fail closed against a blob whose every field is under the attacker's control, because the map is a pure function of ONE field'. tools/harness/w1-21-r2-forge.mjs R8 records the opposite and calls it a LIMIT. R8 is right; A9 is the screenshot. The header is the one the next author will read.

THE BRIEF'S PREMISE IS OVERSTATED AND THE RECORD SHOULD SAY SO. The dispatch describes W1-MAP-r1 C2/D1/D2/D3 as 'presented as four map failures on a walk whose steps never ran'. They were presented as PASSES: W1-MAP-r1.md §1's table lists all four as passing, and §9 records that they first appeared as failures, that critic-w1-map-stepcheck.mjs reproduced the throw with sim.discovery removed entirely, and that preconditions C0/D0 were added so a walk that did not step could not be filed as a map defect. W1-SAVE-AI.json:91 states it correctly ('the critic caught the misattribution, but C2/D1/D2/D3 are worth re-taking'). No false finding was ever published. The re-take was still worth doing and all four survive; the credit belongs to the round-1 preconditions.

corpus_extended.what: S35 forbids 'any square for a place the player has not personally stood in' but says nothing about WHO WRITES the record of where you stood. The whole of this verdict's distance from the gate is that clause meeting a save file the player owns. A ruling is needed on whether an S35 hard fail is a property of the honest path or of every path including a forged save — the builder's w1-21-r2-forge.mjs R8 argues the former in good faith, and both readings are defensible from the text.
corpus_extended.proposed_clause: Name the standard: an S35 map clause is a property of the RUNNING MAP, and a save the player can edit is an input like any other. If that is too strong, say instead that the map must REPORT a footprint it cannot corroborate, which is achievable today from the audit restore() already computes.

method_deviations.what: Wrote my own instruments (tools/harness/critic-map-r2.mjs, critic-map-r2-composite.mjs, critic-map-r2-shots.mjs) rather than re-running only the builder's map-probe.mjs and the round-1 critic's critic-w1-map-r1.mjs. I re-ran both as well.
method_deviations.why: The re-take needed a hostiles-present arm, which neither existing tool has, and the forged-save attack needed the player-facing sealed-file route, which neither attempts. map-probe's forgery check is aimed at a field the loader does not read.

method_deviations.what: Proceeded past `node tools/contention.mjs --gate` exit 3 for the screenshot pass. Every other browser run was preceded by a GO.
method_deviations.why: One browser was the only work left and the frames are gated on their own content rather than on timing. Rule 21 permits this and requires the declaration.

method_deviations.what: The forgery was driven in a live session via importSave() rather than against a cold browser reload.
method_deviations.why: importSave() is the shipping reader either way and a live session is the harder case for the attacker (the world is already built). Recorded as a limit rather than claimed as coverage.

arbitration_questions.question: Is an S35 hard fail a property of the honest path, or of every path including a save file the player has edited?
arbitration_questions.souls_side: Not a Souls/Morrowind axis. The Souls-side habit in this project is that a structural guarantee must hold against a hostile input or it is a convention, and every other capability prohibition here is enforced structurally rather than by trusting a caller.
arbitration_questions.morrowind_side: Morrowind's own map is trivially editable in a save editor and nobody calls that a design failure; the builder's R8 makes exactly this argument and discloses it rather than hiding it. Under that reading the map is compliant and the finding belongs to the save layer.

source_reads.note: Read the wire format (zigzag varint delta trail) in order to deliver a forgery the loader actually parses — a raw bitset decodes to nothing and would have credited the build with a defence it does not have. Afmt proves delivery before any A-result is believed.
Read the draw loop AFTER the pixel measurements, to establish that 'unrendered' is carried by `if (!m.seen(cx,rz)) continue;` rather than by an alpha.
Read after A9 landed, to name what the seal is: an unkeyed sha-256 over the canonicalised body.
Grepped all eight files for map|discovery|__ENGINE|reveal|marker|Discovery before executing anything, so the absence claim is a grep result rather than an inference from a passing probe.

self_audit.self_audit_note: blind_done_where_required is TRUE vacuously: no reference item in scope specifies a blind comparison, and rule 25 forbids me judging a pack I built. FOUR OF MY OWN CHECKS WERE WRONG AND WERE REPAIRED BEFORE FILING, two of which would have been false findings about the build: (1) E3 read placeCount 0 -> 1 after the 'being told' attempts, which was my baseline taken before the first step — the default start position is inside LILMOTH's own pad, so the following steps recorded ground the body was already on; (2) E5 asserted the hover name must be 'Thorn', but the naming element names places[placeIdx], the first place FOUND, i.e. Lilmoth from the spawn; (3) Q4 saw the place list move because tryPlaceMapMarker ends by calling d.observe(4600, 5200) to demonstrate that surplus arguments are ignored, and observe() records the cell the body is in; (4) A12 originally PASSED by matching the substring 'signature' in the save manifest — regionSignature/focusSignature, nothing to do with saves — an inert check that passed for the wrong reason, replaced by the executed arms A12a/A12b. All four are documented in the tools' own comments. The instrument has been shown able to fail three ways plus a control that runs in every mode: --break unrendered reddens U1/U2/U3, --break standing reddens R-D1 in both arms, --break consumer turns G2 GREEN (opposite polarity, because an assertion whose pass condition is 'nothing happened' is worthless until it has been seen to notice something happening), and P3 breaks a live AI back into a plain object and requires the step-fault detector to fire, which it does with the original message.

notes: ORDERING. I read RULES.md, INDEX.md, ARBITRATION S35, W1-MAP-r1.md and the two status files as the dispatch required, so this is not a blind round and I do not claim it is. Everything after that was measured before it was diagnosed: the forgery was delivered before the source was read for the reason it worked, the pixel numbers were taken before the draw loop was read, and the quest tree was grepped before anything was executed against it. CONTENTION: `node tools/contention.mjs --gate` returned GO before every browser run except the screenshot pass (exit 3, declared in method_deviations); one browser per tool run, kept for the whole run, and my own rather than tools/capture/ because every measurement steps the simulation (rule 20). No timing figure appears anywhere in this verdict — every number is a count, a boolean or a pixel colour. NO FILE UNDER game/ WAS EDITED. WHAT I DID NOT DO: travel.visited's coverage is still not isolated (the same gap round 1 declared), the forgery was not tested against a cold browser reload, and the local view's own pixels were not audited — §5's numbers are the world view. FINALLY, AND IT SHOULD NOT BE LOST IN A 3.0: the screen S35 asked for exists and is good. Undiscovered is genuinely unrendered, a square appears only after you have stood somewhere, the name is the place's own name, and there is no marker, route, numeral or travel affordance anywhere on it. The whole distance from the gate is one save field the loader trusts and one object slot nobody froze.
